body.response:
Based on my search, here are the **official MCP (Model Context Protocol) documentation sources** with citations:

## Primary Official Documentation

| Resource | URL | Description |
|----------|-----|-------------|
| **Official Documentation Site** | <https://modelcontextprotocol.io> | Main documentation hub with guides, SDK docs, and client lists |
| **Official Specification (Latest)** | <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest> | Canonical protocol specification with JSON schema and SEPs |
| **Specification (Versioned - 2026-07-28)** | <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28> | Specific versioned spec with RFC2119 compliance keywords |
| **SDK Documentation** | <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/sdk> | Official SDKs for TypeScript, Python, C#, Go, Java, Rust, Swift, Ruby, PHP |

## Source Repositories (GitHub)

| Repository | URL | Description |
|------------|-----|-------------|
| **Main Specification Repo** | <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol> | Schema source (`schema.ts` + `schema.json`), SEPs, and docs |
| **Organization Home** | <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol> | All official SDKs, reference servers, and related projects |
| **TypeScript SDK** | <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk> | Official TypeScript SDK |
| **Python SDK** | <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk> | Official Python SDK |

## Key Facts from Official Sources

- **Created by**: David Soria Parra (@dsp) and Justin Spahr-Summers (@jspahrsummers) at Anthropic (November 2024)
- **Hosted by**: The Linux Foundation (open source, community contributions welcome)
- **Protocol basis**: JSON-RPC 2.0 messages between Hosts (LLM apps), Clients (connectors), and Servers (context/capability providers)
- **Inspired by**: Language Server Protocol (LSP)
- **License**: MIT License

## Official SDKs (Tier 1 - Full Feature Support)
- **TypeScript**: `npm install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk`
- **Python**: `uv add "mcp[cli]"` or `pip install "mcp[cli]"`
- **C#/.NET**: `dotnet add package ModelContextProtocol`
- **Go**: `go get github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`

The official documentation is built with Mintlify and the schema is defined in TypeScript first, then made available as JSON Schema for wider compatibility.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) - Official Documentation Summary

Overview:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems, developed by Anthropic and now maintained under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation. It enables AI applications (like Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor) to connect to data sources, tools, and workflows through a standardized protocol - often described as "the USB-C of AI."

Key Features:
- Standardized protocol using JSON-RPC 2.0 messages
- Enables seamless integration between LLM applications and external data sources/tools
- Supports clients (AI applications), servers (context/capability providers), and hosts
- Vendor-neutral, open specification
- Supports bidirectional, message-driven communication
- Capability negotiation per request

Official Sources:
1. Official Documentation Site: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/
2. Official Documentation (Getting Started): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/getting-started/intro
3. Official Specification (2026-07-28): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28
4. GitHub Organization: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol
5. Main Specification Repository: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol
6. Alternative Documentation Mirror: https://modelcontextprotocol.info/docs

Architecture:
- Hosts: LLM applications that initiate connections
- Clients: Connectors within the host application
- Servers: Services that provide context and capabilities (tools, resources, prompts)

SDKs Available:
- TypeScript (most mature, web/full-stack development)
- Python (data engineering, ML pipelines)
- C# (maintained with Microsoft)
- Visual Inspector tool for testing MCP servers
